statement: Media Cloud should replace Firecrawl as the discovery and source-selection layer, while raw-content hydration remains a separate fetch capability in wave 1.
rationale: The focused source-replacement pass shows that the current Firecrawl contract conflates discovery and content acquisition, while Media Cloud is structurally stronger as a searchable archive and source-selection surface than as a drop-in raw-content scraper.
keyAssumptions: Wave-1 evidence processing still requires durable raw text outside the discovery layer.
A separate hydration step can be introduced without collapsing the existing window pipeline.
validationCriteria: The acquisition design can be expressed as discover, hydrate, then transform.
The engine preserves upstream discovery metadata alongside fetched content.
critiquePoints: Retaining Firecrawl as a hydrator may prolong dependency on it longer than desired.
A better fetcher may need to replace Firecrawl shortly after the split lands.
questions: Should Firecrawl remain the initial hydrator, or should wave 1 budget include a second fetcher immediately?
